title: Robert Lewandowski to leave Barcelona at end of season
content:
Robert Lewandowski has confirmed he will leave Barcelona this season and is set to play his last game at the Camp Nou on Sunday.

Lewandowski, 37, delivered an emotional speech during a training session this week to his team-mates and the backroom staff, highlighting that it has been a pleasure for him to be a part of the club and this Barca squad. He confirmed the news in a social media post on Saturday in which he said “the mission is complete”.

The Poland striker’s next destination is unclear at this stage, but he is set to play his final home game for Barca against Real Betis on Sunday. On Saturday, head coach Hansi Flick confirmed he would start that match.

Lewandowski is in the final year of his contract with Barcelona and The Athletic reported in September that the expectation was for him to leave the club next summer.

“After four years full of challenges and hard work, it’s time to move on,” he said in a post on Instagram. “I leave with the feeling that the mission is complete. Four seasons, three (La Liga) championships.

“I will never forget the love I received from the fans from my very first days. Catalonia is my place on earth. Thank you to everyone I met along the way during these beautiful four years. A special thank you to President Laporta for giving me the chance to live the most incredible chapter of my career. Barca is back where it belongs.”

Speaking in his press conference before the Betis game, Flick said: “The conversation was good. We spoke about that (his exit) and he also had a chat with the team to say goodbye. It’s been a great time for him here in Barcelona.

“I’ve worked with Robert for four years, and we have won nine titles together. It has been a privilege to work with him. He is a professional player at the highest level. Every day he does the best for his body, to be at the highest level. He is a perfect role model for younger players and this mentality is the reason why he can play here now.

“It’s his decision to move now, it can be good for him and also for the club so we can restructure the team a little bit. But I appreciate him a lot for being a fantastic human and a world class player.”

Signing a new striker is a priority for Barca’s board in the summer of 2026, with Ferran Torres often preferred to Lewandowski as the central striker in Hansi Flick’s side this term. Lewandowski has started just 15 of his side’s La Liga games this season as his side successfully defended the league title, and has scored 18 goals across 44 appearances in all competitions.

Barca’s No 1 forward target is Atletico Madrid’s Julian Alvarez, who club sources believe would be keen to join, while recognising negotiations with Atletico could be very tough.

The club are also admirers of Galatasaray striker Victor Osimhen and Chelsea’s Joao Pedro, but it is understood the Premier League side will not entertain any enquiries for the Brazil forward this summer and that he will not be for sale at all.

Asked on Saturday how Barca can replace Lewandowski, Flick said: “We have time. It’s just the end of the season. Now it’s time to say goodbye. He will start tomorrow because he deserves it. What happens next season, we will see. We are looking at the market but there is nothing done. We have time.”

Barcelona signed Lewandowski for a fee rising to €50million ($58m; £44m at current exchange rates) in July 2022 from Bayern Munich. He has made 191 appearances for the club, scoring 119 goals.

He helped Barcelona to win La Liga in his debut season, scoring 33 goals across all competitions and he played a crucial role in his side’s domestic treble last campaign with 42 goals.

Lewandowski previously spent four years at Borussia Dortmund, helping the club to two German titles, before in 2014 joining Bayern, where he won the Bundesliga in each of his eight seasons at the club.

“I still don’t know what I will do,” he told Polish broadcaster Eleven Sports last week. “There are 51 days remaining on my contract, so I still have a bit of time. There is the option of going to a league of a lower level. I am almost 38 (he will turn that age in August) but I feel fine physically and I am considering it. This might be the time to play and enjoy life. I’ll listen to some offers and then make a decision.”

Lewandowski will leave Barcelona with his name being written among the best strikers in the club’s recent history.

The goal return he’s had, 119 in 191 games, has been outstanding — even more taking into account he joined the club aged 33 and arguably past his prime. But what is really going to stand out in the memories of all Barca fans is the moment in which the Poland star decided to join the club.

Barcelona were going through a difficult period, just a year after Lionel Messi’s departure and with a team that was not fighting for major honours, but to qualify for European competitions. The Catalan club were looking for a new player to be the face of the club and Lewandowski, a striker who had everything he could wish for at Bayern Munich, pushed to be that man.

Four years later he is leaving Catalonia with three league titles, having brought Barca back to a Champions League semi-final and having launched a generation that seems destined for big things.

“Barca is back where it belongs,” he said on his statement on social media and it won’t go unnoticed the fundamental role he has played in that.
